state.title: dashboard: EADDRINUSE is a traceback and a restart loop; fail with one line, check the port in doctor and install
state.body:
**Scope** `factory dashboard` binds `ThreadingHTTPServer((args.host, port), Handler)` at `factory/dashboard.py:1001` with no guard. When the port is held — today: a second factory whose `[dashboard].port` fell back to the default 8765 because its host-file entry was written to the wrong path (district#1) — the command dies with a 15-line traceback ending `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and `factory--dashboard.service` restart-loops on it (`Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=5`). After this change: - `dashboard.main()` catches `OSError` with `errno.EADDRINUSE` from the bind and exits 1 with one line on stderr: `factory dashboard: port on is in use; set [repo."".dashboard] port in (each factory needs its own port)`. Other `OSError`s (EACCES for a privileged port, EADDRNOTAVAIL for a bad `--host`) get the same one-line treatment with `strerror`, no traceback. - `factory doctor` gains a row: `dashboard port ` — PASS when the port is free or held by this repo's own `factory--dashboard.service` (`ss -ltnp 'sport = :'` pid vs. `systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value `), FAIL with the holder's process name otherwise. Text and `--json` as for every other row. - `factory install` runs that check before writing units and refuses (exit 1, same message) when the port is held by a foreign process, so a bad port never becomes a restart-looping unit. **Touches** `factory/dashboard.py` (`main()`), `factory/onboard.py` (`doctor()`, `install()`), `tests/`. **Exit gate** - Tests: bind a socket on an ephemeral port in the test, run `dashboard.main(["--port", str(p), "--no-open"])` with `configure` stubbed → returns 1, stderr contains `port

` and the host-file path, no traceback; `doctor` row FAIL when the port is held by a foreign pid, PASS when free; `install` refuses on a foreign holder (systemctl stubbed). - The repo's existing test command passes. - Manual: in `~/dev/mikeroysoft/district`, with rocm-cli's dashboard on 8765, `factory dashboard --port 8765 --no-open` prints the one-line error and exits 1; `factory doctor` shows the FAIL row naming the holder. **Out of scope** Allocating a free port automatically (District owns port allocation, PRD §3); changing the default port.
